answer: A hardware attestation ledger makes each agent prove it runs on a distinct, tamper-resistant chip before joining. At onboarding, the node signs its identity inside a secure element and the ledger records that measurement once, so a second virtual instance fails. Think of a mesa: every plateau is one verifiable plot with a single certified road. A cloud farm pays $40 per legitimized device against $2.50 per spoofed identity, so flooding costs $16 per dollar of fraud. The economy becomes a harbor where honest agents anchor cheaply, and the desert stays a haven for those refusing real silicon.
